newsitem.title: UK: PUNT SLIPS VS MARK IN OTHERWISE DULL CROSS MARKET.
newsitem.headline: PUNT SLIPS VS MARK IN OTHERWISE DULL CROSS MARKET.

text.p: Most mark crosses were sidelined in European trade as they stood back to watch sterling plunge against the dollar and mark, although the Irish punt skidded lower against the mark in line with sterling's weakness.

The pound's freefall of more than five pfennigs on Friday -- amid perceptions there would be no more British interest rate rises for some time -- dragged the punt down by more than four pfennigs from the day's high to a one-month low of 2.6543 marks.
The Irish currency had clawed off the low and was back at 2.6651/01 marks at 1155 GMT, but was still well below its late Thursday European level of 2.6819/69.
Just two weeks ago, the punt traded at its highest level against the mark this decade at 2.7175 marks.

"The Irish punt's rise had been related to sterling's strength and nothing else, and in some ways this drop in the punt comes as a welcome relief to the Irish," said David Brickman, European economist at Yamaichi International.

Irish authorities had been facing a dilemma of needing to raise interest rates to stop the nation's economy from overheating, but not being able to for fear of driving the punt still higher against the marks.
